title: Food Poisoning in Cabo: Symptoms, Treatment & When to Call
description: Food poisoning or traveler's diarrhea in Cabo San Lucas? What helps, warning signs, and how to get a doctor ($199) or IV hydration at your hotel 24/7.

intro: A stomach bug is one of the most common reasons visitors call a doctor in Los Cabos. Usually called food poisoning or traveler's diarrhea, it is unpleasant but most often short-lived. This guide explains what helps, the warning signs that mean you should see a doctor, and how to get care without leaving your hotel.

list: Low-grade fever, chills or body aches
Weakness and dizziness from losing fluids
p_after: Symptoms often start a few hours to a couple of days after eating or drinking something contaminated and commonly improve within one to three days.

list: Sip fluids often — small amounts every few minutes if you are nauseated.
Use oral rehydration salts (sold at every Cabo pharmacy) rather than plain water alone.
Rest, and skip alcohol, coffee and heavy or spicy food until you feel better.
Ask a doctor before taking medicine to stop diarrhea if you have a fever or blood in your stool.

p: See a doctor the same day if you or someone in your group has any of these:
list: Cannot keep fluids down, or very little urine
Dizziness, a racing heart or extreme weakness
Symptoms lasting more than 48 hours, or severe belly pain
A young child, an older adult, a pregnant traveler or someone with a chronic illness who is sick
p_after: Call 911 for confusion, fainting, severe pain or signs of serious dehydration in a child or older adult.

sections.h2: Getting care at your hotel in Cabo

p: An English-speaking doctor comes to your hotel, villa or yacht 24/7, evaluates you, and prescribes medication if appropriate. Typical arrival is 30–45 minutes in Cabo San Lucas. Clinic consultations are $99. Book a doctor.
If you cannot keep fluids down, a nurse-administered IV rehydrates you in about 45–60 minutes. Rapid Hydration is our simplest fluid-and-electrolyte drip; Hangover Rescue adds anti-nausea support.
Oral rehydration salts, probiotics and prescribed medication delivered to your room 24/7, free over $50. Order delivery.

sections.h2: How to lower your risk in Los Cabos
list: Drink bottled or purified water; most resorts serve purified water and ice.
Choose busy restaurants and food that is served hot.
Be careful with raw seafood, salads and fruit you did not peel yourself.
Wash or sanitize your hands before eating.
Pack oral rehydration salts and save a 24/7 doctor's number before you travel.

faq.q: Can I get an IV for food poisoning in Cabo?
faq.a: Yes. If you are dehydrated and cannot keep fluids down, a licensed nurse can give you an IV at your hotel or villa. Our IV drips start at $159 plus tax at your door, or $129 plus tax at our clinic.

faq.q: Do I need antibiotics for traveler's diarrhea?
faq.a: Many cases improve without antibiotics. A doctor can tell you whether you need them; antibiotics require a prescription in Mexico.

faq.q: How fast can a doctor come to my hotel?
faq.a: Typical arrival is 30 to 45 minutes in Cabo San Lucas and the Tourist Corridor, and up to about 60 minutes in San José del Cabo. The visit is $199 USD.

faq.q: Is it safe to drink the water in Cabo?
faq.a: Drink bottled or purified water. Most hotels and resorts serve purified water and ice, but avoid tap water.
